questions.q: What does Neo4j Browser render query results as by default?
options: An interactive graph visualization of the actual nodes and relationships
A CSV file downloaded automatically
A PDF report
Plain unformatted text only, with no other option
questions.explain: Browser's default result view is an interactive graph diagram, though results can also be viewed as a table or raw text/JSON.

questions.q: What does the `:schema` command in Neo4j Browser show?
options: The database's labels, relationship types, and indexes at a glance
The full contents of every node in the database
The Neo4j server's CPU and memory usage
A list of all Cypher keywords
questions.explain: `:schema` gives a quick structural overview of what's already in the database, similar in spirit to checking a database's object list in SSMS.

questions.q: What is the relationship between Neo4j Desktop and Neo4j Browser, per this lesson?
options: Desktop manages database instances and opens Browser against them; Browser is for actually running queries
They are two competing products that do the exact same thing
Browser manages instances while Desktop is only for running queries
Desktop replaces the need for Browser entirely
questions.explain: Desktop is the management layer above Browser — it starts/stops instances and installs plugins, then opens Browser to actually query the running database.

questions.q: What can be installed with one click from inside Neo4j Desktop?
options: Plugins like APOC and the Graph Data Science library
A completely different database engine
SQL Server Management Studio
The Windows operating system
questions.explain: Desktop lets you install plugins like APOC and the Graph Data Science library directly, rather than manually copying files into the plugins folder.

questions.q: What does a Neo4j Desktop "Project" do?
options: Groups related database instances together
Stores a single Cypher query for later reuse
Represents one individual node in the graph
Is a synonym for a Cypher relationship type
questions.explain: Projects in Desktop group related local DBMS instances, for example separate projects per course chapter or per application.
